summary.headline: ENIL FY26 consolidated revenue rose 3.9% to INR565 crore; digital grew 84% to INR112.4 crore while Q4 non-FCT weakened on war-related event disruptions.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue was INR565 crore (+3.9% YoY), with domestic revenue up 4% to INR548 crore led by digital. EBITDA excluding digital was INR76 crore (18% margin) and PAT excluding digital was INR22 crore, which includes a INR17.2 crore one-time gain from reversing deferred tax liability under the Finance Act 2026. Radio faced subdued demand and the Middle East conflict hurt international operations, while non-FCT grew strongly in the first nine months but was hit in Q4 by cancelled international artist concerts. Management reiterated that Gaana should reach breakeven in FY27 and recommended a dividend of INR2 per share.

financial_highlights.value: INR22 crore (includes INR17.2 crore one-time deferred tax reversal)

segments.name: Radio (FCT)
segments.commentary: Demand stayed subdued through FY26 amid macro uncertainty and the Middle East conflict; volume market share cited at 25.2% (25.6% in a later answer). International operations, especially the Middle East, were hit. Q4 FCT revenue was about INR74 crore.

segments.name: Non-FCT (events and experiential)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR148 crore; grew strongly in the first nine months (described as double digit) but Q4 was hit by travel constraints and cancellation of some international artist concerts. Q4 non-FCT revenue was about INR38 crore.

segments.name: Digital (Gaana and pure digital)
segments.commentary: FY26 digital revenue INR112.4 crore (+84%), about 48% of radio revenue. Q4 pure digital revenue about INR29 crore (+61%) per one answer, while Gaana Q4 revenue about INR21 crore (+42%). Gaana revenue has been roughly flat at about INR20 crore in the last two quarters per the analyst; management cited 10-15% sequential growth from INR18 crore to INR21 crore.

guidance_outlook: Gaana: management targets operating breakeven in FY27, with a possibility of achieving it within FY26 itself; quarterly losses have been reduced sequentially.
Gaana subscriber growth expected to continue at about 15% CAGR over the next 2-3 years, with focus on unit economics over subscriber count.
Gaana pricing: annual plan raised to INR799 from INR499; management sees headroom toward a steady-state price of about INR1,200 a year.
Dividend of INR2 per share recommended for FY26; management said the company will keep evaluating inorganic opportunities.
Radio and experiential business expected to recover; management called the Q4 shortfall momentary.
capex_capacity: No capex plans, capacity figures, or commissioning timelines were discussed on the call.
Radio volume market share cited at 25.2% in prepared remarks and 25.6% in a later answer; management said it may have gained some basis points.
Radio inventory utilisation described as roughly flat quarter on quarter in Q4; effective rates (ERs) said to be at similar levels, not up since COVID.

Non-FCT events and experiential business is the capacity-linked segment; Q4 hit by event disruptions, execution delays and cancelled international artist concerts, with recovery expected from the H2-heavy event calendar.
Digital spend reduced 23% YoY in FY26; management said it would keep investing in digital and evaluating inorganic opportunities, with no specific capex amount given.
demand_pricing: Radio demand subdued through FY26 because of macro uncertainty and the West Asia conflict, which weighed on advertiser sentiment.
Gaana annual subscription raised to INR799 (from INR499); music label variable content cost cited at 60-70% of revenue.
Management said customer acquisition costs have risen across the subscription market; CAC and LTV figures were not disclosed.
Management estimates India's paid music subscribers at about 15 million (from about 8 million two years earlier, per EY-FICCI), against a 80-100 million paid-subscription pool across video/OTT.
Competition from free offerings such as YouTube and bundled products was cited; one competitor cut prices sharply in Q3 FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the business plan and subscriber trajectory for Gaana over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 15% subscriber CAGR to continue for 2-3 years, prioritises profitable growth over subscriber count, and sees FY27 as the year to reach breakeven.

qa_highlights.question: Gaana Q4 and FY26 revenue split, and FCT/non-FCT split?
qa_highlights.answer: Digital revenue in Q4 was about INR21 crore (+42%) and INR81 crore for FY26 (+71%). Q4 FCT revenue was about INR74 crore and non-FCT about INR38 crore. Volume growth was described as flat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Gaana revenue look flat over the last two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is seasonal Q3/Q4 churn, that prices were cut and then raised, and that revenue grew about 10-15% sequentially from INR18 crore to INR21 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company disclose CAC-to-LTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share CAC or LTV metrics on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the income tax notice of INR111 crore about?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Ballabh said the notice relates to FY2023-24, with a demand of about INR113 crore after the department passed an order ignoring submissions; the company plans to appeal to the CIT and further authorities and is confident of the outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-line fall about INR15 crore in Q4 and how is radio doing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said radio volume share is about 25.6% and possibly up slightly; the Q4 drop came mainly from non-FCT events after international concerts were cancelled. First nine months of non-FCT grew double digits.

qa_highlights.question: How many paid music subscribers are there and how long to reach the 100 million pool?
qa_highlights.answer: Music paid subscribers are about 15 million per the EY-FICCI report; management said timing depends on behaviour change and could not give a date.

qa_highlights.question: Is cash deployment or inorganic growth planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will pursue profitable growth rather than burn cash, is evaluating inorganic opportunities, and has kept dividends rising.

risks_watch: Income tax demand of about INR113 crore for FY2023-24 under appeal.
Q4 non-FCT weakness from geopolitical disruption and cancelled international artist concerts; watch recovery in events revenue.
Gaana Q4 sequential growth was modest, and CAC is rising; breakeven in FY27 depends on subscriber growth and pricing.
Middle East international radio operations remain disrupted.
Radio industry demand remains weak, with advertiser caution persisting.
Cash of INR424 crore earns returns while radio is valued poorly by the market; capital allocation remains an open question.
summary.management_tone: Confident on digital and Gaana's long-term path and on the tax demand, but cautious on radio and events because of the geopolitical situation. Management avoided disclosing CAC/LTV, branded IP revenue and specific subscriber counts.
key_quotes: We have always believed a music advertising model is a broken model and people should be paying.
We are not here to just run after subscribers if they are not profitable.
So, we are very clear we will chase profitable growth only. We will not just chase numbers.

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; management targets Gaana operating breakeven in FY27 (possibly within FY26), backed by a 23% digital spend cut and a Gaana price increase to INR799, but no capacity, orders or contracts were quantified, and Q4 radio volume growth was flat and non-FCT was hit by event cancellations.
